QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_22

question.text: Ravi Deshmukh, Manager of Shakti Ventures (Cat I), wants to launch a new Liquidation Scheme in 2025 to transfer unliquidated assets of his expiring flagship fund. What does SEBI's April 25, 2024 amendment state about this option?

answer.text: Liquidation Schemes can be freely launched upon mere intimation to SEBI.
Liquidation Schemes require 51% investor approval and filing of a PPM.
Liquidation Schemes are permitted only for Cat III funds.
No AIFs shall launch any NEW Liquidation Schemes post April 25, 2024.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 12: 'Though the modalities for launching of Liquidation Schemes are in place, SEBI has notified that no AIFs shall launch any NEW Liquidation Schemes post April 25, 2024.' The SEBI (AIF) (Second Amendment) Regulations 2024 shut this route. The Trap: Options A, B, C describe a pre-2024 or imagined regime. This is a recent regulatory change frequently missed by candidates using older study material. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C drills the same shutdown rule. Post-2024, the ONLY routes for unliquidated investments are in-specie distribution (with 25% bid rule) OR entering the Dissolution Period with 75% consent.
